articles.title: Hackers Used Meta’s AI Support Bot to Seize Instagram Accounts
articles.summary: Microsoft just dropped a record-breaking 200 patches in one Patch Tuesday, with nearly three dozen rated critical. When even Microsoft can't keep up with their own vulnerabilities, you know the digital apocalypse is accelerating.

articles.title: Alert Fatigue Is Becoming a Security Threat of Its Own
articles.summary: Oracle scrambles to patch CVE-2026-35273 in PeopleSoft as ShinyHunters allegedly exploit it in the wild. Nothing says 'enterprise security' like getting pwned by a crew that sounds like a Pokemon fan club.

articles.title: Casepoint Appoints Paul Colangelo as Chief Executive Officer
articles.summary: Microsoft patches another actively exploited Exchange Server zero-day allowing XSS attacks on Outlook Web Access. Exchange continues its proud tradition of being the gift that keeps on giving—to attackers.

articles.title: Netherlands Seizes 800 Servers, Arrests 2 for Aiding Cyberattacks
articles.summary: Hackers seized the Obama White House and U.S. Space Force Instagram accounts by tricking Meta's AI support bot into password resets via Telegram instructions. AI replacing humans in customer service was always going to end badly.

articles.title: Yes to California's Bill to Ban Surveillance Pricing
articles.summary: CISA contractor 'accidentally' published AWS GovCloud keys and agency secrets on public GitHub while Congress demands answers. When the cybersecurity agency can't secure its own secrets, we're all fucked.

articles.title: Criminal IP at Infosecurity Europe 2026: Introducing AITEM, the Next Chapter of Attack Surface Management
articles.summary: South Korea hammers Coupang with a record $409 million fine for leaking 33+ million customers' data and failing to detect it within 72 hours. Finally, a regulator with teeth who makes privacy violations actually hurt.

articles.title: The Right’s “Election Fraud” Cry for Midterms Previewed in Primaries
articles.summary: EFF demands warrant requirements for Section 702 surveillance as Congress keeps kicking the can down the road. The mass surveillance deadline approaches and our representatives still think warrantless spying is totally fine.

articles.title: ‘News’ Site Keeps Hallucinating EFF Staffers
articles.summary: California considers banning 'surveillance pricing' where corporations charge different prices based on harvested personal data. Because apparently even our shopping receipts need to be dystopian now.

articles.title: A Point-by-Point Breakdown of Trump’s Failed Iran War Objectives
articles.summary: Hakeem Jeffries finally grows a backbone as Democratic leaders rally against extending domestic spy laws. Miracles do happen when the surveillance state gets too obvious to ignore.

articles.title: Microsoft patches record 200-plus vulnerabilities as AI accelerates bug discovery
articles.summary: Former Avast CEO's AI allegedly found every OpenSSL zero-day this year and now runs in air-gapped networks. Either this is the future of vulnerability research or the most elaborate marketing pitch ever conceived.
